name: bloom-filter
description: Bloom filter for boru: a probabilistic set (membership) with no false negatives and a tunable false-positive rate, exposed as the single `Bloom` namespace.
args_order_note: word_specs args are listed in signature order: forward arguments fill them left to right, and the receiver (the last arg) may instead come off the stack.

conventions.import: import "./bloom.aql"  — no `end` needed; the library imports its own boru:* deps, callers need not
conventions.call: forward, receiver LAST (canonical): `Bloom.verb arg... receiver`, e.g. `Bloom.add item bf`. Piping the receiver in from the left (`bf Bloom.add item`) binds identically. Group in parens to use the result as a value, e.g. `(Bloom.contains x bf)`; the parens (or being the complete forward arg of print/def/another verb) terminate the call, so a trailing `end` is usually unnecessary. Receiver-first all-forward (`Bloom.add bf item`) matches no signature: `boru check` reports uncalled_function and `boru X` (which checks first) does not run. Exception: Bloom.merge takes two BloomFilters, so `Bloom.merge a b` is legal and merges a INTO b — the last argument is always the receiver.
conventions.construct: build filters ONLY via Bloom.make; treat BloomFilter fields as read-only and mutate through the namespace words
conventions.mutation: add and merge MUTATE the receiver in place and return the SAME object — there is no immutable copy
conventions.probabilistic: contains => false is certain (the item was definitely never added); contains => true is probabilistic (false-positive rate ~ p)
conventions.count_vs_added: count is a cardinality ESTIMATE, not a tally; the exact insert count is `added` (read via encode or bf.added)
conventions.import_resolution: relative to the directory of the importing file (for both `boru X` and `boru check X`), not the working directory — a test in test/ imports "../bloom.aql"
conventions.errors: failures raise coded errors caught with `do [...] error [...]`; read a bound error as e.code / e.message, or in the handler (error on the stack) with a quoted key: get "code" / get "message" (get evaluates its key, so a bare `get code` is undefined_word). Codes: bad_input (Bloom.make args missing or out of range), incompatible_merge (Bloom.merge filters disagree on m or k), bad_payload (Bloom.decode text is not an encode snapshot)
conventions.serialization: encode produces a jsonic snapshot; decode rebuilds an equivalent filter from it (round-trips n, p, m, k, added, and every set bit). Snapshots are portable across processes on the same module version, not across versions that change the hashing.
conventions.known_defects: boru main @ 64c5ab2: a program that also imports boru:test can see `type_error: <word>: return value 1: expected BloomFilter, got BloomFilter` from the words that return a filter (boru:test mints its record types from a fresh type-ID counter, colliding with BloomFilter's ID). See dx-report.md.

BloomFilter.note: sealed class; construct only via Bloom.make; fields are read-only. `bits` is a FlexList of 63-bit integer words.

make.note: n = expected distinct items; p = target false-positive rate in (0, 0.5]. Derives m (bit count) and k (hash count). Raises bad_input on a non-integer/non-positive n or a p outside (0, 0.5]. `{n, p} Bloom.make` is the same call.

add.note: MUTATES bf and returns the SAME object. Any value; stringified internally. Sets k bits, increments added.

contains.note: false = definitely never added; true = probably added (false-positive rate ~ p).

count.note: ESTIMATE of distinct items, not a tally. Empty filter => 0. O(m/63).

merge.note: Union of b into the receiver a (the LAST argument; piping form `a Bloom.merge b`). MUTATES a and returns it; b is unchanged. Requires identical m and k (same (n, p)); else raises incompatible_merge. O(m/63). Both args are BloomFilter, so a reversed order is not rejected — it merges the other way.

encode.note: jsonic snapshot (params + set-bit indices). Round-trips through Bloom.decode. O(m).

decode.note: Rebuild a filter from a Bloom.encode snapshot; independent of the original. Raises bad_payload on unparseable or incomplete text.
